name: VITA shade guide

lead: The VITA shade guide is a set of tooth-coloured tabs used to name how light or dark teeth are, from A1 to D4.
It is a measurement reference, so it is used in studies and in forum talk to record whitening progress.

paras: A clinician holds tabs next to the tooth and picks the closest match by value and chroma; instruments can also measure colour.
It carries no risk itself. Studies report coverage gaps in shade guides and differences between visual and instrument readings.

lead: The VITA classical shade guide is a set of tooth-coloured tabs, labelled A1 to D4, used by dentists to describe and match tooth colour. It is arranged by value (lightness) and chroma (colour intensity).[1] In whitening and cosmetic dentistry it serves as a reference scale for stating how light teeth are before and after treatment.

Studies in dental research have examined its limitations, including colour coverage errors and the accuracy of visual shade matching compared with instruments.[2][3] In appearance communities, shade numbers are used as shorthand for how white teeth are.
infobox: Shade matching and whitening outcome records

paras: Researchers frequently use the guide to measure bleaching results, for example by enrolling volunteers with teeth at shade A3 or darker and counting shade steps gained.[4] Wikipedia notes in-office bleaching commonly gives 2 to 7 shades and at-home strips or trays about 1 or 2.[1]

Studies have evaluated the guide as a measurement tool. A 1991 study examined coverage errors of two shade guides, and a 1998 study compared a sphere spectrophotometer with human evaluation of tooth shade.[2][3] ClinicalTrials.gov lists small trials comparing visual, photographic and spectrophotometric shade matching.[5][6] Clinical bleaching trials use the guide as an outcome scale.[4][7]
